2026-10-28 — Agent loop no-progress recovery, informed by OpenClaw loop detection. `runReadOnlyAgentLoop` now compares the bounded outcome tuple (tool ID, normalized arguments, bounded result) against the preceding 16 successful attempts. - Harness/runtime change: the LFM3 planner no longer receives an empty `anyOf` schema during required tool stages. After an exact read, only the required final action is offered; its native function schema is flat and validated by the application. The context-aware budget and registry-residency regressions passed in the focused 217-test set. Details: [agent-loop design](AGENT-LOOP-DESIGN.md) and [test evidence](TEST-RESULTS.txt).

- Context-window configuration (updated 2026-10-29): the pinned LFM3 Q4/Q8 setting now offers 8K/16K/32K/64K/128K/256K, with the existing 8K default preserved. Inspected custom GGUFs can select up to the larger LFM3 choices only when the declared architecture is LFM3; other adapters remain capped at 32K. The selected value is validated against the model context and passed through the app manifest to Wllama `n_ctx`. The UI warns that larger contexts may exceed device memory. Liquid AI publishes 256K model context, but no browser WebGPU allocation, fit, prompt, speed, quality or sustained run at those lengths has been proven. This removes an application policy cap; it is not a device-capability claim.

- Agent extensibility gate: executable custom `tool.js` packages are restricted to local read-only/compute capabilities and no network. The model can already propose Memory capture/edit through final app actions and the existing review UI; those are not custom executable tools, and commits still use the canonical revision/confirmation path. Missing capabilities are effect-declared custom write proposals, user-enabled online connectors, and MCP transport. Keep these distinctions explicit; see [agent-loop design](AGENT-LOOP-DESIGN.md).
- Model residency / UX gate: the shared execution manager keeps one inference role resident at a time. Same-identity requests can reuse the resident engine. Registry synchronization replaces/unloads an engine only when its own registration changes; editing an unrelated backend no longer evicts the active engine. Controlled router tests cover both cases. This does not prove that iOS Safari keeps a worker/model resident through suspension, OS eviction or app updates. No real load timings or device-memory fit were measured on build `290e157cd54d979d`. The latest PC snapshot was about 1.30 GiB free, below the comparison preflight, so no weights were loaded. See [model execution tests](../design/prototype/tests/model-execution.test.mjs), [router tests](../design/prototype/tests/text-engine-router.test.mjs), and the [resident reuse evidence](TEST-RESULTS.txt).

  Design boundary: `planDialogueMessages` tells the planner to select knowledge answering for new facts after sourced answers, while the calculator accepts only an explicit arithmetic expression. A tool receipt verifies arithmetic, not whether the model chose operands from the right source; the current calculated-only response in `submission-workflow.ts` also records no sources. A complete solution needs a typed proposed calculation with explicit operand-to-source ranges and units; validate the exact pinned source revisions and numeric interpretation, reject ambiguity or changed sources, execute the registered calculator, and persist both citations and the checked receipt. Test conflicting and multiple values, Japanese numerals, stale/retracted sources, rounding, mixed write requests and cancellation. Merely allowing the malformed `chat` response or prompting the model to invent an expression would not establish that link.

  Existing `validateGroundingRefs` can enforce active, current, exact source text and eligible lineage, but it cannot prove that a number in an excerpt is the quantity the user meant. Operand binding therefore needs an explicit proposal and a clarification/review path when the relationship or unit is ambiguous; a valid arithmetic receipt alone is insufficient. No unconnected numeric extractor or speculative automatic answer has been added.

  Additional boundary to change: both the model-selected `calculate` branch and the calculator-only agent result branch in `submission-workflow.ts` currently finish with `refs: []`; neither proves a model-selected operand came from the prior cited answer. A future source-bound operation must not enter either branch as if its receipt alone were grounding. The observed failed turn did not reach those branches; this is a code-review finding, not a reproduced incorrect answer. Preserve support for independently stated calculations while adding explicit source/operand provenance and tests.
